meta.description: Designs genomics experiments so technical nuisance variation is balanced against biological variables, using constrained designit assignment, hidden-batch detection with SVA, and explicit routing for downstream correction.
meta.audit_type: final-pass Phase 2 re-audit: seven regression inputs plus two new validation inputs
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numeric results are from labelled synthetic audit inputs and their saved execution logs; no citation, clinical result, or statistic was invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill provides experimental-design and analysis-boundary guidance only; it makes no individual diagnostic, treatment, or prescribing conclusion.

methodological_ground.detail: Fresh runs confirmed the central methodological boundaries: a confounded ComBat covariate is rejected, an estimable condition-plus-batch model fits partial imbalance, and the balance checker warns or stops rather than silently accepting a bad layout.

code_usability.detail: All four shipped R files parse. Each substantive workflow produced and checked its expected layout or analytical result. The non-zero package-session teardown is a designated-environment stability defect recorded under T1, not a syntax, dependency-resolution, or algorithmic failure in the shipped code.

functional_suitability.note: The exact tip covers constrained assignment, bridge-channel layouts, balance verification, SVA missing-value handling, correction boundaries, and reproducibility metadata.

reliability.note: Shared validation clearly rejects missing columns, over-capacity layouts, confounding, and invalid channel coordinates; an operational-exit failure in the designated R environment prevents full marks.

performance_context.note: The scripts are focused and seeded, but their documented full 10,000-iteration optimization can take minutes and emits an environment-level non-zero termination.

agent_usability.note: Commands, required columns, balancing variables, hard stops, soft warnings, and downstream ownership are explicit.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers and a short usage guide cover assignment, confounding, hidden batches, and method choice.

security.note: No credentials, destructive operations, or raw-code execution are present; command arguments are ordinary local file and scalar parameters.

maintainability.note: Runnable concerns are separated into assign_batches.R, bridge_layout.R, and one shared check_balance.R; all copied source files parsed successfully.

agent_specific.note: The Skill has precise triggers, routing, seeds, and escape hatches. Its full execution still depends on repairing the supplied R environment.

inputs.label: Assign 24 samples to three batches while balancing condition and sex.
inputs.note: The exact copied command wrote a 24-row layout with condition and sex both 4/4/4 across batches, then R exited by segmentation fault after completion.
inputs.execution_note: Executed run/in1_assign_canonical.sh under crispr-screen-analyst; checked layout24.csv and run/in1_assign_canonical.out.

assertions.text: The documented assignment command produced a layout CSV.
Condition is balanced across all three batches.
Sex is checked as an additional balanced covariate.
The successful result is not silently accepted without a validation table.

inputs.label: Assign 60 samples across four TMT 16plexes while reserving channel 16 for a bridge sample.
inputs.note: The copied bridge command reserved channel 16 and wrote the layout; condition was 7/7/8/8 and the checker correctly warned that site spread was 2. R then segfaulted after output completion.
inputs.execution_note: Executed run/in2_bridge_canonical.sh; checked layout60.csv and run/in2_bridge_canonical.out.

assertions.text: The requested bridge channel remains unassigned to biology.
No plex exceeds its 15 non-reserved biological positions.
Condition is represented in every plex.
Avoidable site imbalance is surfaced rather than hidden.
assertions.note: The shared checker warned of a largest-minus-smallest spread of 2.

inputs.label: Estimate hidden batches from an intensity matrix that contains missing values.
inputs.note: The copied shipped example reported 282/24000 missing cells, restricted to 766 complete rows, estimated one surrogate variable, and reduced the visualization-only ComBat PC1-batch correlation from 0.48 to 0.01 before R segfaulted on teardown.
inputs.execution_note: Executed run/in3_sva_na.sh, which calls run/test_sva_missing.R and the copied examples/batch_design.R; checked run/in3_sva_na.out.

assertions.text: Missing values are reported before SVA is called.
Only complete observations enter the Option A SVA estimate.
A hidden factor is estimated on the complete matrix.
assertions.note: The example estimated one surrogate variable.

assertions.text: Batch-cleaned data are framed as visualization-only.
assertions.note: The shipped output explicitly labels the PC comparison as plots only.

inputs.label: Check balanced, avoidably unbalanced, and fully confounded layouts before sequencing.
inputs.note: The shared verifier accepted a balanced condition/sex layout, emitted the expected soft warning for a spread of 3, and rejected a condition-by-batch confound.
inputs.execution_note: Executed run/in4_balance_cases.sh calling run/check_balance_cases.R; checked run/in4_balance_cases.out.

assertions.text: Balanced layouts are accepted.
assertions.note: Condition and sex tables are all 4/4/4.

assertions.text: The soft imbalance warning fires above a spread of one.
Fully confounded layouts halt.
assertions.note: The test captured the documented confounded-layout error.

assertions.text: All requested covariates are checked.
assertions.note: Both condition and sex were supplied to check_balance.

inputs.label: Test whether ComBat can rescue a perfectly confounded design and whether partial imbalance remains estimable with batch in the model.
inputs.note: On labelled synthetic matrices, ComBat rejected a covariate perfectly aliased with batch and limma fit condition plus batch without NA coefficients for partial imbalance; R then segfaulted on teardown.
inputs.execution_note: Executed run/in5_combat_claims.sh calling run/test_combat_design_claims.R; checked run/in5_combat_claims.out.

assertions.text: A biological covariate perfectly confounded with batch is rejected by ComBat.
assertions.note: The synthetic call raised a confounding error.

assertions.text: Partial imbalance is estimable when batch is retained in the model.
The test does not claim that correction rescues a non-identifiable design.
assertions.note: It explicitly tests and confirms rejection.

assertions.text: The data are identified as synthetic.
assertions.note: The test script is a seeded synthetic regression check.

inputs.label: Repeat the same 24-sample assignment with the same seed and compare output bytes.
inputs.note: The repeated 10,000-iteration run wrote layout24_repeat.csv and it was byte-identical to layout24.csv, but again ended in the reproducible R teardown segmentation fault.
inputs.execution_note: Executed run/in6_determinism.sh; independently compared SHA-256 values of layout24.csv and layout24_repeat.csv after the script returned non-zero.

assertions.text: The repeated documented command produced a second layout.
The same seed produces identical layout bytes.
assertions.note: The two CSV SHA-256 hashes are equal.

assertions.text: The repeated layout retains condition and sex balance.
The process exits successfully after a valid result.
assertions.note: R ended with a segmentation fault after writing the result.

inputs.label: Request balancing on a missing covariate column.
inputs.note: The command rejected missing_sex.csv with the explicit required-column message; the harness correctly treated that rejection as success.

assertions.text: A missing requested covariate is rejected.
The error identifies the required input contract.
assertions.note: It names id and every requested feature variable.

assertions.text: No misleading layout is emitted.
The harness records the expected rejection correctly.
assertions.note: The wrapper returned PASS after the rejection.

inputs.label: Try to place 60 samples into only 24 batch positions.
inputs.note: The assignment command stopped before optimization with the exact more-samples-than-slots message; no output layout was created.

assertions.text: Over-capacity inputs are rejected before optimization.
The failure identifies the capacity problem.
assertions.note: It states more samples than n_batch x n_position slots.

assertions.text: No partial layout is emitted.
The harness treats expected validation rejection as a passing outcome.

inputs.label: Reserve channel 17 in a 16-channel plex.
inputs.note: designit rejected the out-of-range channel coordinate before an invalid bridge layout could be written; the wrapper correctly passed the expected rejection.

assertions.text: Out-of-range reserved channels are rejected.
assertions.note: designit reported a value outside the channel dimension range.

assertions.text: The failure occurs before a layout can be emitted.
The error is actionable for a caller.
assertions.note: It identifies the channel dimension as invalid.

assertions.text: The expected validation rejection is captured as a successful test.

key_strengths: The exact branch tip now has reusable, parsed scripts for constrained assignment, bridge layouts, and shared balance checking.
Every design boundary tested is explicit: missing covariates, capacity overflow, confounding, and invalid bridge coordinates are stopped instead of silently repaired.
The SVA example reports and handles missing values before calling SVA, and the correction tests respect the non-identifiability of perfect confounding.
The same seeded assignment produced byte-identical layout output across two full optimizer runs.

recommendations.title: The designated crispr-screen-analyst R environment segfaults after designit or sva workflows complete
recommendations.problem: Five substantive valid workflows wrote correct, checked artifacts but exited non-zero with a segmentation fault. A fresh minimal probe that only loads designit reproduced the same teardown failure, while a parser-only probe for all shipped R files exited normally.
recommendations.root_cause: The failure is reproducible in the dispatched environment after package loading and is outside the source worktree; it is not explained by syntax, an absent package, or an invalid input.
recommendations.fix: Repair or replace the R/designit runtime in F:/OpenScience/audit-envs/crispr-screen-analyst under the environment tooling policy, prove a clean library(designit) session exits 0, then rerun this Phase 2 audit. No source-only edit can make a successfully completed R process return 0 in this environment.
